# upgrade

Moves the store to the latest format this build writes, which takes free-form branches and tags; irreversible, older releases do not open it afterwards. On a store of that format already it changes nothing.

```yaml
title: "upgrade"
description: "Upgrade the store format."
since: "0.4.0"
mutates: true
identity_required: false
cli_command: "swarmops upgrade"
envelope_op: "upgrade"
request_type: "UpgradeReq"
annotations: {"destructiveHint":true,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false,"readOnlyHint":false}
max_result_chars: null
```

## Input schema

`arguments` is a `UpgradeReq`: `swarmops schema UpgradeReq` prints the type. A field the type does not know is ignored.

It takes no fields: pass `{}`.

### JSON Schema

As `tools/list` gives it: each `$ref` replaced by its definition, so that it stands alone.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "description": "`upgrade`: move the store to the latest format this build writes. It cannot be undone:\nolder releases do not open the store afterwards.",
  "title": "UpgradeReq",
  "type": "object"
}
```

## Annotations

It removes or rewrites store files that the journal and the objects stand for, and moves no ref and records nothing. Run again, it finds its work done.

| Annotation | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `destructiveHint` | `true` | True: a tool that changes the store may overwrite or delete what is there, not only add to it. |
| `idempotentHint` | `true` | True: calling it again with the same arguments changes nothing more. |
| `openWorldHint` | `false` | True: it reaches beyond a closed set of things. Every tool here stays inside the store. |
| `readOnlyHint` | `false` | True: the tool does not change its environment, the store. |

Its entry in `tools/list` carries no `_meta`.

## CLI command

[`swarmops upgrade`](../commands/upgrade.md) runs the same operation and prints the same envelope.

## Return information

A tool result: the envelope, whose `op` is `upgrade`, as `structuredContent` and again as the text of its one `content` block. `isError` is true exactly when the envelope's `ok` is false. On success the envelope's `result` is what [`swarmops upgrade`](../commands/upgrade.md#return-information) returns.

## Errors

A failed call is a tool result with `isError: true`; the envelope's `error.code` is one of the [error codes](../errors.md).

- [`E_INVALID_ARG`](../errors.md#e_invalid_arg): arguments that do not fit `UpgradeReq`, a field named twice among them included, or that break one of the server's own rules.
- [`E_NOT_A_REPO`](../errors.md#e_not_a_repo): the server's store is not there; the server serves on.
- [`E_INTERNAL`](../errors.md#e_internal): the operation panicked, a bug.

Then the errors of the operation, as [`swarmops upgrade`](../commands/upgrade.md#errors) lists them.
